Title: Update a slot start time to one minute before an existing slot's end time (boundary case for overlap)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There are two existing slots: MORNING (09:00-12:00) and AFTERNOON (12:00-17:00).
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Slot Management screen. 2. Select the MORNING slot. 3. Update the start time to 11:59. 4. Save the changes.

Test Data: Start time: 11:59, End time: 12:00 (existing AFTERNOON slot)
Expected Result: An error message is displayed: 'Slot overlaps with an existing slot. Please adjust the time.' The MORNING slot remains unchanged (09:00-12:00).

Title: Update a slot end time to one minute after an existing slot's start time (boundary case for overlap)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There are two existing slots: MORNING (09:00-12:00) and AFTERNOON (12:00-17:00).
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Slot Management screen. 2. Select the AFTERNOON slot. 3. Update the end time to 09:01. 4. Save the changes.

Test Data: Start time: 12:00 (existing AFTERNOON slot), End time: 09:01
Expected Result: An error message is displayed: 'Slot overlaps with an existing slot. Please adjust the time.' The AFTERNOON slot remains unchanged (12:00-17:00).

Title: Set a new slot with start time one minute before an existing slot's end time (boundary case for overlap)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There is an existing MORNING slot (09:00-12:00).
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Slot Management screen. 2. Click 'Add New Slot'. 3. Set the start time to 11:59 and end time to 15:00. 4. Save the new slot.

Test Data: Start time: 11:59, End time: 15:00
Expected Result: An error message is displayed: 'Slot overlaps with an existing slot. Please adjust the time.' The new slot is not created.

Title: Set a new slot with end time one minute after an existing slot's start time (boundary case for overlap)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There is an existing AFTERNOON slot (12:00-17:00).
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Slot Management screen. 2. Click 'Add New Slot'. 3. Set the start time to 10:00 and end time to 12:01. 4. Save the new slot.

Test Data: Start time: 10:00, End time: 12:01
Expected Result: An error message is displayed: 'Slot overlaps with an existing slot. Please adjust the time.' The new slot is not created.

Title: Update a shop holiday with a date exactly at the current date and time (boundary: current timestamp)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There is an existing holiday for the shop with a future date. Current date and time is 2023-11-01T14:30:00.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Shop Holiday Management screen. 2. Select the existing holiday. 3. Update the holiday date to 2023-11-01T14:30:00. 4. Save the changes.

Test Data: Holiday date: 2023-11-01T14:30:00 (current timestamp)
Expected Result: The holiday is updated successfully. A success message is displayed: 'Holiday updated successfully for shop [shop name]'. The holiday date is set to 2023-11-01T14:30:00.

Title: Update a shop holiday with a reason of exactly 1 character (boundary: minimum length)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There is an existing holiday for the shop.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Shop Holiday Management screen. 2. Select the existing holiday. 3. Update the reason to 'A'. 4. Save the changes.

Test Data: Reason: 'A' (1 character)
Expected Result: The holiday is updated successfully. A success message is displayed: 'Holiday updated successfully for shop [shop name]'. The reason is saved and displayed as 'A'.

Title: Update a shop holiday with a reason of 0 characters (boundary: empty string)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop admin. There is an existing holiday for the shop.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Shop Holiday Management screen. 2. Select the existing holiday. 3. Clear the reason field. 4. Save the changes.

Test Data: Reason: '' (empty string)
Expected Result: An error message is displayed indicating that the reason cannot be empty. The holiday is not updated.

Title: Retrieve all areas with custom page size of exactly 2 (boundary: small page size)
Preconditions: User is logged in as an admin. There are at least 3 areas in the system.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Area Management screen. 2. Set the page size to 2. 3. Click 'Retrieve Areas'.

Test Data: Page size: 2
Expected Result: HTTP status code 200 (OK). Response body contains a paginated list of areas with exactly 2 items on the first page, including pagination metadata (totalPages, totalElements, size=2, number=0).

Title: Retrieve all areas with custom page size of 999 (boundary: very large page size)
Preconditions: User is logged in as an admin. There are at least 1000 areas in the system.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Area Management screen. 2. Set the page size to 999. 3. Click 'Retrieve Areas'.

Test Data: Page size: 999
Expected Result: HTTP status code 200 (OK). Response body contains a paginated list of areas with up to 999 items on the first page, including pagination metadata (totalPages, totalElements, size=999, number=0).

Title: Retrieve all areas with custom page number of 1 (boundary: second page)
Preconditions: User is logged in as an admin. There are at least 11 areas in the system. Default page size is 10.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Area Management screen. 2. Set the page number to 1. 3. Click 'Retrieve Areas'.

Test Data: Page number: 1, Page size: 10 (default)
Expected Result: HTTP status code 200 (OK). Response body contains a paginated list of areas with the 11th item (if exists) on the second page, including pagination metadata (totalPages, totalElements, size=10, number=1).

Title: Upload a photo with a file size exactly at the maximum allowed limit (boundary: max file size)
Preconditions: User is logged in. Maximum allowed file size is 5 MB.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Photo Upload screen. 2. Select a photo with size exactly 5 MB. 3. Set userId to 1. 4. Click 'Upload'.

Test Data: File size: 5 MB, userId: 1
Expected Result: HTTP status code 201 (Created). Response body contains the created photo with userId 1 and no workerId.

Title: Upload a photo with a file size one byte above the maximum allowed limit (boundary: max file size + 1)
Preconditions: User is logged in. Maximum allowed file size is 5 MB.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Photo Upload screen. 2. Select a photo with size 5 MB + 1 byte. 3. Set userId to 1. 4. Click 'Upload'.

Test Data: File size: 5 MB + 1 byte, userId: 1
Expected Result: HTTP status code 400 (Bad Request) or 500 (Internal Server Error). No photo is created or updated.

Title: Request OTP with an email address containing a space (boundary: invalid format)
Preconditions: User is on the OTP request screen.
Steps:

Test Data: Email: 'user @example.com' (contains space)
